newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Europe precious metals narrowly mixed, quiet.
newsitem.headline: Europe precious metals narrowly mixed, quiet.

text.p: Precious metals opened narrowly mixed in quiet European trade as the market waited to see if U.S. funds would resume aggressive gold sales, dealers said.

"We are seeing some buying interest around $341," one dealer at a big Swiss bank said, noting short-selling by U.S. funds yesterday had failed to push gold under $340. "I think $340/341 should be the bottom for the short run," he said.
Gold was quoted at $341.25/$341.75, down 25 cents an ounce from the close in London.
Platinum firmed one dollar to $364/$365 vs $363/$364, while palladium eased to $149.25/$150.25 from $150.20/$151.20.

One dealer said the market largely shrugged off yesterday's news that South Africa's Amplats, the world's largest platinum producer, intended to boost annual output to around 2.1 million ounces from 1.8 million.
